derivation_notes: The parent already couples instantaneous allele frequency and delayed feedback through q, but assumes only linear-plus-quadratic prevalence dependence in the inhibitory factor. Here that law is refined by adding a higher-order joint term q*p**3 so suppression remains weak near rarity yet steepens disproportionately once the favored allele is common.
change_summary: I relaxed the assumption that feedback-induced inhibition has only low-order dependence on prevalence at fixed q. The successor keeps the same states and q dynamics but changes the scored mapping dp_dt(p,q) by adding a biologically plausible late-stage self-crowding/interference term.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Feedback-induced inhibition grows smoothly as a linear-plus-quadratic function of favored-allele frequency at fixed q.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Threshold-free but steepening commonness-dependent interference: once the favored allele is common, accumulated niche depletion, social antagonism, or self-crowding can intensify faster than the parent low-order form permits.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Set frequency_dependence_steepening = 0 to recover the parent law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed q, the parent makes the realized selection term decline with p through a denominator that is only linear-plus-quadratic in p, so inhibition strengthens smoothly with no distinct onset scale beyond those low-order terms.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the low-order feedback assumption so the inhibitory effect of accumulated feedback q on the favored allele steepens disproportionately once p is already common, creating stronger late-stage curvature in dp_dt as a function of p even when q is held fixed.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar early q but increasing p into the common-allele regime, the child shows a later, sharper suppression of dp_dt than the parent; the parent can match early or late decline with one parameter set, but not both if the slowdown turns on more abruptly at high p.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when q is appreciable and p reaches moderate-to-high values away from 0, so delayed feedback has accumulated and common-allele inhibition can steepen; weak when q is near its relaxed minimum or p remains rare throughout observation.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the same mechanism appears as modest extra bending of dp_dt over intermediate p; in holdout with larger attained q or longer runs reaching higher p, the stronger late-stage suppression becomes clearer.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the added higher-order dependence of feedback on p vanishes, leaving only the existing linear and quadratic p terms in the inhibitory factor.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Threshold-free but steepening commonness-dependent interference: once the favored allele is common, accumulated niche depletion, social antagonism, or self-crowding can intensify faster than the parent low-order form permits, even without introducing a new state.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a new joint p-q dependence that is negligible at low p but increasingly important at high p, changing curvature rather than just global gain or a simple rescaling of existing terms.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The inhibitory factor depends on favored-allele prevalence through only linear and quadratic powers of p at fixed q.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The inhibitory factor includes an additional higher-order prevalence term that acts jointly with accumulated feedback q, producing stronger late-stage suppression when the favored allele is common.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For the same supplied p and q, the child preserves near-parent dp_dt when p is small but depresses dp_dt more strongly once p becomes moderate to high, especially when q is appreciable. This is a direct change in the target mapping dp_dt(p,q), not only a change in the auxiliary q trajectory.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can only rebalance the existing q*p and q*p**2 contributions, which changes suppression smoothly across all p. It cannot simultaneously keep early-to-mid p growth relatively high while creating an extra late high-p bend tied specifically to the joint state q*p**3; fitting q trajectories alone does not remove this mismatch because the scored derivative is evaluated conditional on the observed p and q.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when q is appreciable and p reaches moderate-to-high values away from 0, so delayed feedback has accumulated and common-allele inhibition can steepen; weak when q is near its relaxed minimum or p remains rare throughout observation.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the same mechanism appears as modest extra bending of dp_dt over intermediate p; in holdout with larger attained q or longer runs reaching higher p, the stronger late-stage suppression becomes clearer.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the added higher-order dependence of feedback on p vanishes, leaving only the existing linear and quadratic p terms in the inhibitory factor.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that accumulated ecological/social feedback erodes the favored allele's advantage with only low-order dependence on its current prevalence, missing a biologically plausible sharper crowding or antagonism effect once the allele becomes common.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Feedback-induced inhibition grows smoothly as a linear-plus-quadratic function of favored-allele frequency at fixed q.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Threshold-free but steepening commonness-dependent interference: once the favored allele is common, accumulated niche depletion, social antagonism, or self-crowding can intensify faster than the parent low-order form permits, even without introducing a new state.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to keep the same states but relax the parent's specific low-order shape for how prevalence and accumulated feedback combine in the target mapping dp_dt(p,q). The parent already includes delayed feedback via q, but at fixed observed q it still imposes a single smooth phase of suppression as p increases. Vary p along observed trajectories while holding the parameter set fixed and considering runs where q has become moderate through its existing dynamics. Under these admissible conditions, the child would predict near-parent behavior when p is small, then stronger downward curvature in dp_dt once p is moderate to high, reflecting disproportionately stronger inhibition in common favored types. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely the auxiliary q trajectory, because for the same supplied p and q the instantaneous dp_dt becomes different. A single refitted parent parameter set can rescale or mildly rebalance early-versus-late suppression through its existing p and q terms, but it cannot create a distinctly sharper late-stage bend across conditions where early growth remains relatively high and only high-p regimes are strongly compressed. The effect is scientifically visible only if observations reach sufficiently high p and nontrivial q; if trajectories stay near rarity or q remains small, the refinement collapses effectively back toward the parent.

scenario_text: A large haploid population carries two alleles at one locus, and one allele has a constant viability advantage. Its frequency changes continuously as differential reproduction amplifies the favored type while the diminishing supply of the alternative type slows further change. The allele frequency is the sole dynamic state, with the other allele represented by its complementary frequency. The benchmark targets the instantaneous rate of change of the favored allele frequency along this trajectory.
